title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 3 close: Augustine — gratuitous election before merits; Hypognost. 6
pass_a_gloss: Finally, we say that this is the very sentence which Augustine everywhere defends against the Pelagians, namely, That men are elected gratuitously, and before all foresight of merits, not only to the gifts of grace, but also to the kingdom of glory: however they be brought to the kingdom of glory by the way of good works, or of merits, as the ancient Fathers are wont to speak. I will cite only one place, which stands thus: From the damnable mass of the human race God foresaw by mercy, not by merits, those whom by election of grace he predestined to life, Contra Pelagianos Hypognosticon book 6. Where you see that that foresight on which predestination to life rests is not of our merits, but of the divine mercy, who decreed to elect us from the damnable mass to participation of eternal life, and to adorn us with merits.
pass_b_english: Finally, this is the very sentence Augustine everywhere defends against the Pelagians: men are elected gratuitously and before all foresight of merits — not only to gifts of grace but also to the kingdom of glory — however they are brought there by the path of good works or merits, as the ancient Fathers usually speak. One place only: From the damnable mass of the human race God foresaw by mercy, not merits, those whom by election of grace he predestined to life (Contra Pelag. Hypognost. 6). So the foresight on which predestination to life rests is not of our merits but of divine mercy, who decreed to elect us from that damnable mass to share eternal life and to adorn us with merits.
source_text: Postremo, dicimus hanc esse ipsissimam sententiam quam Augustinus passim propugnat contra Pelagianos, nimirum, Eligi homines gratuito, & ante omnem praescientiam meritorum, non modo ad dona gratiae, sed etiam ad regnum gloriae: utcunque perducantur ad regnum gloriae per viam bonorum operum, sive meritorum, ut loqui solent antiqui Patres. Unicum tantummodo locum citabo, qui sic se habet, De damnabili humani generis massa Deus praescivit misericordia, non meritis, quos ex electione gratiae praedestinavit ad vitam, Contra Pelag. Hypognost. lib. 6. Ubi videtis praescientiam illam, qua nititur praedestinatio ad vitam, non esse meritorum nostrorum, sed misericordiae Divinae, qui decrevit nos eligere ex massa damnabili ad participationem vitae aeternae, atque meritis ornare.
